edge.title: Muon lr 0.02→0.025 and wd 0.01→0.0125; 3500 steps
edge.summary: Hyperparameter-only retune of #1: Muon lr and weight decay are both scaled by 1.25 (lr=0.025, wd=0.0125), raising the per-step decoupled shrinkage lr·wd from 2e-4 to 3.1e-4 at peak, and the run is shortened by 100 steps to 3500. Optimizer code, aux AdamW, schedule and init are unchanged; evidence is one pre-rules run.

changes.label: Muon lr/wd scaled ×1.25
changes.detail: optimizer2 = Muon(lr=muon_lr, weight_decay=muon_weight_decay) with muon_lr=0.025, muon_weight_decay=0.0125 (was 0.02/0.01); lr·wd rises from 2e-4 to 3.125e-4 per step at peak.

changes.label: train_steps 3600 → 3500
changes.detail: Claimed step equals the scheduled end (single run, 3.2767 at 3500).

edge.parent_check: Consistent: the diff vs #1 touches only train_steps and the Muon lr/wd.
edge.noise: The values are hoisted into module constants muon_lr / muon_weight_decay (later scripts inline the literals again).

techniques.note: as #1: all 'proj' params (incl. LM head) zeroed

hparams.init.hidden_std: torch default nn.Linear U(±1/sqrt(fan_in)), std ≈ 0.0208 (q, k, v, mlp.fc)
hparams.init.proj: zero (attn.proj, mlp.proj and LM head weights)
hparams.init.bias: torch default U(±1/sqrt(fan_in)) for q/k/v/fc; proj biases zero

caveats: Single run (3.2767, n=1) recorded before the significance rule (README: 'My first three results failed to follow this rule'); 3.28 − 3.2767 = 0.0033 < 0.004. Git history shows this config (with the literals inlined) was the train_gpt_simple.py baseline from 2026-04-26 until the #6 refactor.
